books.section: Great Depression and the New Deal (1929-1939)

stimulus.text: Senator Huey Long of Louisiana, photographed in 1935 seated at a desk in front of shelves of law books, gesturing with both hands as he speaks. Long built a national following with his Share Our Wealth program, which proposed capping large fortunes and guaranteeing every family a homestead and a minimum income.
stimulus.source_note: Huey Long at desk, 1935 press photograph. Public domain; via Wikimedia Commons.

source: original; stimulus photograph by an unknown press photographer, 1935, public domain
stem: Long's Share Our Wealth program, described in the passage, called for which of the following?

options.text: Ending all federal relief programs at once
options.misconception: Long demanded more government action, not less; ending relief was the conservatives' position, not his.

options.text: Capping large fortunes and guaranteeing a minimum income
Cutting taxes on incomes over 50,000 dollars
options.misconception: Cutting taxes on high incomes was what business critics of the New Deal wanted; Long wanted steep taxes on the rich.

options.text: Banning labor unions from American industry outright
options.misconception: Long built his following by promising help to ordinary people, not by banning unions.

rationales.A: Background from the books: Long attacked Roosevelt for doing too little, so ending relief is the opposite of his program.
rationales.B: Background from the books: Share Our Wealth proposed capping personal fortunes and guaranteeing every family a homestead and a minimum income, paid for by taxes on the rich.
rationales.C: Background from the books: Long wanted steep taxes on large fortunes, not tax cuts for high incomes.
rationales.D: Background from the books: nothing in Long's program banned unions; his appeal was to poor and working people, not against them.
rationales.general:
1. The passage says Long proposed capping large fortunes.
2. It also says he guaranteed every family a homestead and a minimum income.
3. Both parts move wealth from the rich toward ordinary families.
4. That is redistribution, not an end to relief or a tax cut for the wealthy.
Remember: name the direction of a proposal first, toward more sharing or toward less government.
